text.en: Applicative verbs constitute approximately one third of all verbs in Ainu, representing up to 7% of the entire Ainu lexicon ⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--applicative-verbs-constitute-approximately-one-third-of-all⟧. Across all three applicative markers *ko-*, *e-*, and *o-*, applicatives derived from intransitive bases are far more numerous than those derived from transitive bases ⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--in-ainu-applicatives-derived-from-intransitive-bases-are⟧. Inherently locative object verbs such as *oma-re* are limited in number, whereas the applicative prefixes *e-* and *o-* can be added productively to any semantically compatible base, especially in verse ⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--inherently-locative-object-verbs-like-oma-re-are⟧. In Southwest Hokkaido, unaccusative intransitive verbs can host the applicative prefixes *e-*, *ko-*, and *o-* ⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--so-called-unaccusative-intransitive-verbs-in-ainu-can⟧, as seen in derivations like *e-ray* 'die at some place' from *ray* 'die' and *o-rer* 'sink into sth' from *rer* 'sink' ⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--applicative-prefixes-in-ainu-can-attach-to-certain⟧. However, applicatives formed from internally caused verbs of change of state do not occur in Southwest Hokkaido ⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--applicatives-formed-from-internally-caused-verbs-of-change⟧. Oblique relations are frequently promoted to applicative direct objects and then relativized by means of a gap strategy ⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--oblique-relations-are-frequently-promoted-to-applicative-direct⟧. In Southwest Hokkaido, applicative morphology appears much more frequently in poetic genres such as *yukar* and *kamuy yukar* than in colloquial speech or prose oral literature ⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--applicative-morphology-is-used-much-more-frequently-in⟧. Bugaeva proposes that in colloquial Ainu and prose oral literature of Southwest Hokkaido, where applicatives are used less frequently, they encode greater discourse salience ⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--in-colloquial-ainu-and-prose-oral-literature-applicatives⟧. In the poetic genres of oral literature in the Shizunai dialect, applicatives are likewise not infrequent ⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--in-the-poetic-genres-of-oral-literature-in⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語において適用詞動詞は全動詞の約3分の1を占め、語彙全体の最大7%に達する⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--applicative-verbs-constitute-approximately-one-third-of-all⟧。3つの適用詞標識*ko-*、*e-*、*o-*のすべてにおいて、自動詞語幹から派生した適用詞動詞は他動詞語幹から派生したものよりもはるかに多数存在する⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--in-ainu-applicatives-derived-from-intransitive-bases-are⟧。*oma-re*のような本来的な場所目的語動詞の数は限られているが、適用接頭辞*e-*および*o-*は意味が適合する任意の動詞に生産的に付加でき、特に韻文において顕著である⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--inherently-locative-object-verbs-like-oma-re-are⟧。北海道南西部においていわゆる非対格自動詞は適用詞*e-*、*ko-*、*o-*を取ることができ⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--so-called-unaccusative-intransitive-verbs-in-ainu-can⟧、*ray*「死ぬ」からの*e-ray*「〜で死ぬ」や*rer*「沈む」からの*o-rer*「〜に沈む」のように一部の非対格動詞への付加が実在する⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--applicative-prefixes-in-ainu-can-attach-to-certain⟧。一方、北海道南西部において内在的に引き起こされる状態変化動詞からの適用詞派生は生じない⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--applicatives-formed-from-internally-caused-verbs-of-change⟧。斜格関係は適用詞構文の直接目的語として現れることが多く、空所化方略によって関係節化される⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--oblique-relations-are-frequently-promoted-to-applicative-direct⟧。北海道南西部では、ユーカラやカムイユーカラといった韻文ジャンルにおける適用詞形態論の使用頻度は、口語や散文の口承文芸よりもはるかに高い⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--applicative-morphology-is-used-much-more-frequently-in⟧。Bugaevaの提案によれば、適用詞の使用頻度が低い北海道南西部の口語や散文口承文芸において、適用詞はより高い談話の顕著性を標示しているとされる⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--in-colloquial-ainu-and-prose-oral-literature-applicatives⟧。静内方言の口承文芸の韻文ジャンルにおいても適用形は稀ではない⟦claim:valency/applicative-system-overview--in-the-poetic-genres-of-oral-literature-in⟧。
